findings.text: follow-on: the reason check precedes the self._stopped early return, so stop() is idempotent for a valid reason but raises ValueError for a bad reason even on an already-stopped host. Every production caller passes a module constant, so this is a residual of the guard's placement, not a defect -- moving the isinstance check after the self._stopped return, or only validating on the first stop, would make idempotence unconditional.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the two SessionHost.stop call sites (session_host.py:592 in the supervise finally, session_host.py:633 in run()'s finally); both pass a reason. The other '.stop()' hits (cli.py:5615 poller.stop, serve.py:3957 _EXECUTED_SOURCE.stop) are unrelated classes.
item_verdicts.diff: read the two commits gained since review (e5a14599c fix + two tests + evidence fragment; 8ed54b97b pins the refusal regex) against base 242220970.
item_verdicts.done_when: read §13's done-when; the raised-loop and refusal tests were added since the last review, the two prior tests (bare request_stop, end-of-file) remain, and the manifest's gate logs 26 passed EXIT=0 at head.
item_verdicts.goal: read §13 and the node brief; the incremental diff makes the unnamed raised-loop exit record _FAILED_REASON and enforces the reason at runtime, both in service of §13's 'every stop path names its reason'.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; baseline 22 / after 26 both EXIT=0, two-arm negative control EXIT=1, revisions e5a14599c and 8ed54b97b beyond the reviewed base.

justifications.durability: Each new test fails when the guard it exercises is removed (both mutations verified), so the tests fire rather than passing vacuously; the runtime ValueError makes a null or empty reason unrepresentable rather than merely unannotated, which is exactly what the prior review named as the residual.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced on a full scratch copy of head 8ed54b97b (module.__file__ under the scratch tree): the two-file gate logs 26 passed EXIT=0, matching the run's gate.log. The four new tests pass, and two mutations each redden the test they guard -- restoring the unconditional signalled fallback fails test_a_raised_loop_records_a_reason_and_propagates (records 'signalled', not 'host failed'), and removing the isinstance guard fails test_stop_refuses_a_reason_that_is_not_a_non_empty_string (DID NOT RAISE ValueError). The run's own arms agree: baseline.log 22 passed EXIT=0, gate.log 26 passed EXIT=0; added failures 0.
justifications.fit: _FAILED_REASON (session_host.py:101) sits beside _SIGNALLED_REASON / _REQUEST_ENDED_REASON / _EXITED_REASON with a comment stating the mechanism; the supervise finally comment names the two unnamed exits; no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in code, comment or message.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/plans/a-follower-lives-as-long-as-its-session.html:167 (§13) requires every stop path to name a reason. This increment closes the last unnamed exit: the supervise finally at reckon/crew/session_host.py:590-592 records _SIGNALLED_REASON only when a stop was requested and _FAILED_REASON (session_host.py:101) otherwise, and stop() (session_host.py:489-490) refuses a reason that is not a non-empty string before any state change, so host.stop(None) can no longer write stop_reason: null. It also retires the prior review's only follow-on.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses the existing stop() / _write_record stop_reason machinery and the reason-constant convention; no second stop path, no new abstraction.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 242220970..8ed54b97b changes exactly the three declared write paths (reckon/crew/session_host.py, tests/test_session_host.py, docs/evidence/fragments/.../a-stopped-host-names-its-reason.html); no path outside the brief's scope is touched.
